features.description: Project detector: from a repo root produce a deterministic ProjectProfile of languages, package managers, build systems, test frameworks, app frameworks, docs/ADR presence, and infra/config surfaces. Pure, no network, graceful on an empty or unknown repo.
features.acceptance: a pure detector scans a repo root and returns a ProjectProfile listing detected languages, package managers, build systems, test frameworks, app frameworks, docs/ADR presence, and infra/config surfaces; it is deterministic (same repo -> same profile), performs no network or mutation, and degrades to an empty-but-valid profile on an unknown or empty repo. ProjectProfile's detection classes form a CLOSED, enumerated list (languages, package_managers, build_systems, test_frameworks, app_frameworks, docs_adr, infra, config) that F004's evidence-type mapping is required -- and tested -- to cover totally, so no detected class can be invisible to coverage. The detector's traversal is BOUNDED on large repos via a deterministic scan cap (no unbounded walk); reaching the cap is recorded as a truncation signal on the profile, not silently dropped. A test asserts determinism (same repo -> identical profile) AND that a synthetic over-cap repo trips the bounded-traversal cap and stamps the truncation signal.

features.description: Extractor registry mapping evidence-kind/language to an extractor and its availability, tier-aware (tier 0 filesystem / tier 1 heuristic / tier 2 parser / tier 3 build-runtime), so the system can list available vs missing extractors for a given ProjectProfile.
features.acceptance: a registry resolves, for a given ProjectProfile, which extractors are available and which are missing per evidence-kind/language, each tagged with its tier (0 filesystem, 1 heuristic, 2 parser, 3 build/runtime); a detected language with no parser-backed extractor is reported as having a missing higher-tier extractor while still being served by the tier-0/tier-1 ones. Registry resolution is PURE and DETERMINISTIC: the same ProjectProfile yields the same availability/missing result, with no network or mutation. A test asserts determinism (same profile -> identical resolution) and that resolution touches no filesystem/network.

features.description: Tier-0 inventory graph (dirs, package/build/config manifests, test dirs, docs/ADRs; low/medium confidence) for ANY repo, plus Tier-1 heuristic import-pattern edges for common languages emitted low-confidence/unresolved unless a relative target resolves; contract-stamped, deterministic, bounded, never dropped.
features.acceptance: build produces a baseline graph for any repo: tier-0 nodes for directories, package/build/config manifests, test dirs and docs/ADRs (contract-stamped, low or medium confidence), and tier-1 heuristic dependency edges for common languages that are low-confidence unresolved endpoints unless a relative target resolves; the scan is deterministic and bounded and never silently drops an edge. When the bounded scan hits its cap, the graph emits an EXPLICIT truncation/limit-hit marker (scan_truncated, with the cap and what was reached) so a capped, partial graph is never presented as complete — the omission is surfaced, not silent. Even for an empty or trivial repo the baseline yields a NON-EMPTY tier-0 graph (at minimum a repo-root directory node) — never an empty graph. A test asserts a synthetic over-cap repo trips the cap and stamps scan_truncated on the graph. RENDER-TRUTH PASSTHROUGH: an acceptance test asserts against the FINAL operator-facing build_view_state/render payload (after any render-truth gating) that tier-1 low-confidence/unresolved edges, tier-0 filesystem/config nodes, and the scan_truncated marker SURVIVE to the rendered payload unchanged — the render gate must not filter them out before the operator sees them.

features.description: Tiered coverage block: overall rollup (limited/partial/covered) + per-language status (covered/missing_extractor/not_found) + per-evidence-type status keyed by ONE taxonomy unified with the architecture contract's source_kind enum (filesystem/code/manifest/build/test/config/infra/doc/adr/runtime), with a total mapping from every ProjectProfile detection class, pinned deterministic rollup rules, and honest confidence ceilings, computed on project registration and inside build_view_state.
features.acceptance: build_view_state emits a coverage block with an overall rollup, a per-language map (covered / missing_extractor / not_found) and a per-evidence-type map. ONE TAXONOMY: the evidence_type enum is unified with the architecture contract's existing source_kind enum — filesystem (NEW source_kind for tier-0 directory inventory), code (imports), manifest (package manifests), build (build-system files), test, config, infra, doc, adr, runtime — no parallel vocabulary; external/unknown are endpoint classifications and are excluded from coverage keys. Every ProjectProfile detection class maps deterministically into exactly one evidence_type via a single exported mapping table (languages->code, package_managers->manifest, build_systems->build, test_frameworks->test, app_frameworks->manifest, infra->infra, config->config, docs_adr->doc/adr), and a test asserts that mapping is TOTAL over ProjectProfile's closed detection-class list so no detected class is invisible or silently folded into filesystem. PINNED ROLLUP (deterministic lattice): overall is 'limited' when NO detected language has parser-backed (tier-2) imports coverage (the empty repo included); 'covered' only when EVERY detected language is parser-backed covered AND no detected evidence class reports missing_extractor or error AND the scan was not truncated; 'partial' otherwise. runtime (tier-3, reserved) always reports not_found in C0 and never demotes the rollup; an evidence class the detector did NOT detect reports not_found WITHOUT demoting; scan_truncated demotes an otherwise-covered rollup to partial. Tests pin each rollup rule (empty repo -> limited; pure-Python -> covered; Python+Swift -> partial; truncated otherwise-covered -> partial). A repo with an unextracted language still shows its filesystem/package graph AND a clear low-confidence dependency note. covered semantics are explicit: a parser-backed (tier-2) language reports its imports evidence_type as covered at observed/high confidence and is NEVER downgraded to heuristic/low; a heuristic-only (tier-1) language reports imports partial at low confidence; each per-evidence-type entry carries the tier it was satisfied at. An integration test drives the real project-registration/build_view_state path so detection -> registry resolution -> baseline construction -> coverage computation are proven to run together (operator-outcome), not just as isolated units. When the underlying scan was truncated (scan_truncated set), the coverage block SURFACES that limit-hit signal in the FINAL operator-facing view-state payload (the render-truth gate must not filter it) so a capped scan never reads as fully covered; a test asserts a truncated scan is reflected in the rendered coverage block, not hidden.

features.description: Fixture-repo tests across Python, JS/TS, and Swift/Kotlin asserting the weak baseline renders for each, imports are heuristic-low for unextracted languages while filesystem/package coverage is present, and the coverage block flags the missing Swift/Kotlin extractor without suppressing the tier-0 graph.
features.acceptance: EVERY fixture case — Python, JS/TS, Swift/Kotlin, empty_repo, and over-cap (truncated) — is driven through the REAL project-registration + build_view_state operator path, with assertions made on the final view-state payload; low-level baseline-builder unit tests may supplement but do NOT satisfy this acceptance on their own. Through that path: each fixture yields a non-empty tier-0 graph; for Swift/Kotlin the coverage block reports a missing parser extractor and dependency confidence low while still presenting filesystem/package nodes; for Python/JS the existing parser-backed coverage is preserved (no regression). The empty_repo case asserts a non-empty tier-0 graph (repo-root node) with overall coverage 'limited', and asserts Python/JS imports remain covered/high (not downgraded) while Swift/Kotlin imports are heuristic-low. The over-cap case asserts the bounded scan trips its cap, the graph stamps scan_truncated, and the rendered coverage block surfaces the truncation (never reads as complete).
